findings.evidence: Prefer rg over grep because it is faster and respects .gitignore — a preference the model already applies.
findings.fix: Keep the availability gate and the codebase-memory-mcp rule; move the generic rg/fd/bat/sd/eza preference rows to a recorded drop or a one-line pointer, since the model produces those substitutions unprompted.

findings.evidence: Only two NEVER items sit in the early landmine section; the rest of the reasons live in a later table the agent may not treat as gotchas.
findings.fix: Point the early NEVER section at the Hard rules table by name and add the two non-obvious dispatch gotchas (do not renumber reviewers.json after dropping a native entry; a pending lane keeps RUN_TMP_DIR) so the reasons sit where the loop starts.

findings.evidence: Description names frameworks and --cross-ai but not the near-miss it must not take: code review, PR review, or writing a new plan.
findings.fix: Use when a design, spec, requirements, or plan document needs review-and-fix before the next step. Framework-aware across superpowers, GSD, OpenSpec, Spec Kit, Kiro, BMAD, and generic docs — orchestrates a reviewer and routes fixes via the appropriate handler (native framework skill, slash command, or direct-edit fixer), with optional cross-AI reviewer dispatch via --cross-ai/--no-cross-ai. Respects worktrees, scopes to lifecycle stage, loops until approved or iteration cap. Triggered by ai-kit-spec-review, review my spec/plan, naming one of these frameworks alongside a spec/plan/design review, or passing document path(s). Not for reviewing pull-request diffs, scoring a SKILL.md, or writing a new plan from scratch.

findings.evidence: cross-ai-dispatch.md is a mandatory full-file read on every run, including --no-cross-ai, and it also holds Step 1, pending-lane, and cross-repo sections that only some runs need.
findings.fix: Keep points 0–2 as the unconditional read. Split Step 1 subprocess rationale, the pending-lane section, and declared-paths into files the matching branch names, and say not to load them on a session-default or --no-cross-ai run.

findings.evidence: Probe-quota is told both to walk the ladder and that two parts of that walk are not owner-ruled yet, with no default for what to do when they happen.
findings.fix: State the default: walk the shipped ladder, name the two extra cases in the Step 5 message, and do not invent a different fallback. Leave the owner-rule note as the reason, not a second choice.

findings.evidence: Thirteen evals assert routing and config-status wording; none checks a real review report, a fixer edit, or a Status line produced by running the loop.
findings.fix: Add one eval whose input is a flawed plan and whose assertions check the reviewer's Status line and that the routed fixer changed the file, beside the existing routing cases.

findings.evidence: Ten should-trigger and ten should-not-trigger queries, but no train/validation split.
findings.fix: Mark about 60% of the queries train and the rest validation, keeping both labels in each split, and revise the description only from train failures.

findings.evidence: The parser prog is review-spec, so --help does not document the ai-kit-spec.py entry the skill tells the agent to run.
findings.fix: Set the parser prog to ai-kit-spec.py and add a one-line usage example per subcommand the skill invokes (config-status, dispatch-reviewer, merge-reports).

findings.evidence: Issues Found? goes to Surface on its no edge, while Step 2 sends every Issues Found line to the cap check and only a non-Issues status ends the loop.
findings.fix: Delete that edge. Route every Issues Found status into Iter < cap?, and keep Surface for Approved, Failure, and No Status line only.

findings.evidence: Variant ids (none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max, thinking) are dated 2026-11-19 but the source is a seen API response, not a vendor doc URL or a live read.
findings.fix: Point the list at the recorded opencode help or model API fixture and the date it was captured, and tell the agent to re-read GET /api/model rather than trust the stored ids.
